summary.headline: Thomas Cook Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell 12% YoY to INR 21,530 million and PBT fell 21% to INR 885 million, driven by Middle East exposure.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income was INR 21,530 million, down 12% YoY, with PBT of INR 885 million, down 21%, mainly from Desert Adventures and DEI in the Middle East. Excluding the GCC subsidiaries, group EBIT grew 8%, and India businesses (forex, MICE, corporate travel, domestic) were stable to growing. Sterling Holidays reported its best quarter ever, with revenue up 21% and EBITDA up 21%. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, though it said H2 should be better than H1 if conditions hold.

segments.name: Foreign exchange
segments.commentary: Segment revenue +6% YoY, EBIT +8%, EBIT margin 45.3%. Retail turnover +8% YoY vs industry travel forex decline of ~8% (LRS Apr-May); education turnover +36%, digital penetration 23.5% vs 20.4%.

segments.name: Travel (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 17,106 million, -14% YoY; EBIT INR 405 million, -50%. Domestic +29%, short-haul +6% (+21% excluding Middle East), long-haul sales -28%. MICE +14% to INR 5,420 million; DMS -31% to INR 5,422 million with Desert Adventures revenue -89%.

segments.name: Sterling Holidays
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1.7 billion (+21%), EBITDA over INR 620 million (37% margin), PBT margin 28% (+200 bps). Occupancy 77% (+700 bps), ARR INR 7,809 (+10%), RevPAR +20%; net debt-free with cash above INR 3.7 billion.

segments.name: DEI (Digital Imaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,307 million vs INR 2,097 million; EBIT swung to INR -152 million from INR 106 million. About 50% of global business is in the Middle East; China site closures and Bahamas contract end added pressure. Net assets employed INR 243 crore.

segments.name: Desert Adventures (GCC)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 89% YoY; management estimated its EBIT impact at roughly INR 8-9 crore (about INR 90 million), not confirmed. Cost base did not flex as fast as volumes.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 guidance given; management said it is too early to forecast full-year outcome and cannot confirm double-digit earnings growth.
Travel EBIT margin working range of about 4-5%; long-term take rates across B2B and B2C around 14-15%.
If conditions remain constant, H2 FY27 expected to be better than H1.
DEI cost optimisation benefits expected in Q2 and Q3 FY27; Middle East recovery sub-20% in Apr-Jun, about 30-35% in July.
DEI long-term target: 20% ROE; normal-year DEI EBIT margin about 6-7% of sales.
Long-haul deficit narrowed from about 28-30% to slightly lower levels in recent weeks; July and early August conversion better than Apr-Jun.
capex_capacity: Sterling: over 78 resorts, hotels and retreats with nearly 3,800 rooms in 65+ destinations; visible pipeline of 35+ properties and more than 2,000 rooms; asset-right model of owned, leased and managed.
DEI: technology upgrade completed in recent years; management said ongoing capex is low and the platform should last 5-10 years; net assets INR 243 crore.
Forex: new counters at Delhi Airport Terminals 1 and 2; branch network being optimised; airports entered opportunistically, not as a strategy.
demand_pricing: Forex travel turnover declined alongside the industry, but education turnover grew 36% with NBFC partnerships and Study Buddy Card launch.
Corporate travel gross turnover above INR 7 billion, +15% YoY; net revenue INR 350 million, +7%; 7 new accounts added.
MICE: over 110 groups; 77% international and 23% domestic; demand deferred from earlier quarters translating into business in June.
Sterling ARR +10% to INR 7,809 and occupancy +700 bps, indicating demand ahead of supply additions.
Short-haul ATV is 20-25% lower than long-haul, creating a mix headwind on revenue.
Management said margins are under pressure from higher airline costs and forex; tactical pricing used to keep capacity engaged.
TCS rate cut to 5% has had no visible impact on pricing; management called it a cash outflow, not a price change.

qa_highlights.question: How did underlying outbound leisure demand trend in July and early August, and do short-haul destinations carry comparable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said July and early August conversion was better than Apr-Jun but too early to call a shift. Short-haul margins are similar to long-haul, though short-haul ticket values are 20-25% lower.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thomas Cook pursue more airport forex counters over branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Airports are opportunistic, not a strategy; entry is made only at commercially rewarding terms, as with Delhi Airport.

qa_highlights.question: DEI: what are capital employed, normalised EBIT and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Net assets INR 243 crore; normal-year EBIT margin 6-7%; target 20% ROE. Major technology upgrade done, with periodic upgrades roughly every 10-12 years.

qa_highlights.question: Travel FY27 topline and EBIT margin outlook, and the TCS impact on pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 guidance. Internal EBIT margin range 4-5%. Management said it saw no clear TCS pricing benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the double-digit earnings growth guidance still achievable, and what is the split of GCC subsidiary impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not confirm double-digit growth. DEI EBIT moved from INR 10 crore profit to INR 15 crore loss (INR 25 crore delta). Detailed numbers to be obtained from Investor Relations.

qa_highlights.question: Will DEI cost optimisation show in Q2 results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visible benefits in Q2 and Q3 FY27; revenue recovery in the Middle East will determine earnings quality.

risks_watch: Middle East exposure: DEI is about 50% of global business in the Middle East; April-June Middle East recovery was sub-20%, July about 30-35%. Revenue recovery is the swing factor for H2 earnings quality.
Desert Adventures cost base did not flex as fast as volumes; cost optimisation benefits at DEI are expected in Q2 and Q3 FY27, to be verified in the Q2 print.
No FY27 guidance; management could not confirm double-digit earnings growth, and the long-haul deficit (about 28-30% in Q1) must narrow further for H2 to beat H1.
Short-haul mix headwind: ticket values 20-25% lower than long-haul, and margins under pressure from higher airline costs and forex; Travel EBIT working range 4-5%.
Desert Adventures and DEI GCC-impact figures were not fully disclosed on the call (Desert Adventures EBIT impact about INR 90 million, unconfirmed); detailed split deferred to Investor Relations.
Geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia conflict) continues to drive customer booking hesitancy; July and early August conversion better than Apr-Jun but not yet confirmed as a trend.
key_quotes: Excluding the GCC-based subsidiaries, (DEI and Desert Adventures), the consolidated results of the group registered a growth of 8% at an EBIT level for the quarter, highlighting the resilience of our underlying businesses.
I really don't have an answer to say what will be my full year forecast at this point in time, given the environment which we operate in currently.

But just alluding to the point that I made previously to the question that was asked by Chetan, I think from a long-haul perspective, we are seeing some positive shift in the trend, that is, that whatever deficit that we were seeing previously, the deficit percentages have come down.
So honestly, to be very frank, I haven't seen a big impact coming out of the TCS.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on India businesses, Sterling and forex, and openly cautious on FY27 outlook, declining to give full-year guidance and calling the Middle East outlook too uncertain to forecast. It was candid on DEI and Desert Adventures underperformance, while being evasive on the GCC EBIT split and on whether double-digit earnings growth remains achievable.
